conventions.convention: Schreier graphs use right cosets Hg and positive x-edges Hg→Hgx; traversing such an edge backward reads x^{-1}.
In the right-coset convention the Schreier generator is s(t,x)=tx·overline(tx)^{-1}; inverse letters are rewritten as s(overline(tx^{-1}),x)^{-1}.
A Schreier transversal consists of reduced right-coset representatives; a Schreier system is additionally closed under every initial segment, including the empty word.
For a finite or enumerated countable free basis, shortlex representatives are used; for an arbitrary basis the stated construction assumes the Axiom of Choice to well-order it.
Left translation on bounded functions is (g·f)(x)=f(g^{-1}x), and amenability means existence of a mean invariant for this left action.
An (S,ε)-Folner set is finite and nonempty and satisfies |sF△F|<ε|F| for every s∈S; the Folner condition quantifies over every finite S, including the empty set, and every ε>0.
On this page a Folner sequence is indexed by n≥1 for a fixed enumeration G={g1,g2,…}, and requires vanishing relative symmetric difference for each fixed enumerated element.
A paradoxical decomposition is a finite pairwise-disjoint partition into A-pieces and B-pieces such that specified left translates of each subfamily separately partition the whole group.
R[G] is the free left module on G for a commutative ring R, consists of formal finite sums, and writes the basis vector indexed by g as [g].
Every representation on this page is finite-dimensional; irreducible additionally means the underlying space is nonzero and has only 0 and itself as subrepresentations.
A splitting field for the fixed finite group G is defined locally by End_G(V)=k, meaning every endomorphism of every irreducible k-representation is scalar.
The image of f is ker(coker f), while the coimage is coker(ker f); the arrows belonging to those kernel and cokernel constructions are part of the convention.
The working definition of an abelian category is: additive, every morphism has a kernel and cokernel, and every canonical coimage-to-image map is an isomorphism.
The page intends Grothendieck's AB1 to mean existence of kernels and cokernels and AB2 to mean invertibility of coimage→image; additivity is a standing unnumbered hypothesis.
Exact functor means additive and both left exact and right exact; left exactness is preservation of finite limits and right exactness preservation of finite colimits.
Subobjects are mutual-factorisation classes of monomorphisms ordered by factorisation; quotient objects are classes of epimorphisms with the dual, reversed orientation.

load_bearing.statement: An abelian category is an additive category in which every morphism has a kernel and a cokernel and every canonical comparison coim(f)→im(f) is an isomorphism.

Assume the ultrafilter lemma. A group G is amenable if and only if it satisfies the Folner condition; amenability-to-Folner is claimed to use only the invariant mean, while the converse spends the ultrafilter extension.

For finite or enumerated countable X, shortlex least right-coset representatives form a Schreier system; assuming Choice, the same holds for arbitrary X after well-ordering. For a system obtained in either way, its nontrivial Schreier generators form a free basis of H≤F(X).

For a commutative ring R, a group G, and a left R-module M, compatible R-linear G-actions and compatible left R[G]-module structures correspond inversely; an R-linear map is G-equivariant if and only if it is R[G]-linear.
For every f:A→B in a category with kernels and cokernels, there is a unique overline(f):coim(f)→im(f) satisfying i_f·overline(f)·q_f=f.
In an abelian category, every monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel, and dually every epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel.

For a commutative ring R and group G there is a unique R-bilinear multiplication on R[G] with [g][h]=[gh]; it makes R[G] a unital R-algebra with identity [e], and every [g] is a unit with inverse [g^{-1}].

concerns.concern: Step 2.1 miscomputes the fourth Schreier generator for T={1,ab}. It is s(ab,b)=ab²(ab)^{-1}=aba^{-1}, not a. The actual first and fourth generators are inverses, so the intended redundancy conclusion is salvageable, but the displayed list and the asserted relation aba=a·b·a are false as written.

The amenable⇒Folner direction is not established. Step 1.2 invokes an undefined finite-dimensional separation of the normalized indicators of all finite subsets; for an infinite group their span contains all singleton indicators and is not finite-dimensional. No precise separating functional or contradiction with the invariant mean is derived.

Step 1.1 never supplies the actual A_i, B_j pieces or their translating elements. Saying that first-letter classes 'determine' two translated copies does not verify either of the two exact partition equalities required by the cited definition.

The verification repeats the preceding theorem's unexpanded 'first-letter partition' and depends on that theorem, but still gives no pieces or translations. It therefore does not independently exhibit the paradoxical decomposition claimed by the example.

The proof asserts, without a cited lemma or derivation, uniform cardinality comparison and a boundary-neighborhood inclusion for thickened quasi-isometric images. Those estimates are the substantive theorem; merely stating them does not prove that Folner ratios transfer.

The pointwise-limit dependency distinguishes chosen pointwise limits from mere existence and explicitly spends Choice to select the latter over a small object set. This theorem assumes only that the target is abelian and silently chooses a kernel and cokernel at every source object, so its stated choice boundary is incomplete.

The proof obtains small boundary only for the chosen generating set S, then immediately claims the full Folner condition, which quantifies over every finite subset of G. A reader can close this by expressing a finite test set as words of uniformly bounded S-length and shrinking the generator tolerance accordingly, but that step is absent.
Step 1.1 defines M=max_{s∈S}||s||∞ without treating S=∅, although the Folner condition explicitly allows an empty finite test set. The empty case is immediate but missing.
The verification takes M=max_{s∈S}|s| for an arbitrary finite S without handling S=∅. The claim remains true vacuously in that boundary case.
The verification takes M=max_{s∈S}||s||∞ for an arbitrary finite S without handling S=∅. The claim remains true vacuously in that boundary case.

Step 3.1 infers non-finite generation merely from having displayed an infinite free basis. It should add the elementary finite-support argument showing that no finite subset can generate all those basis elements; an infinite displayed basis alone is not the stated argument.

The example calls the subgroup infinite-rank immediately after displaying an infinite free basis, but the opened rank definition is deliberately restricted to finite bases. The finite-support argument proving that no finite generating set exists is omitted.

Step 3.1 says the edge Hg→Hgx is 'the same edge' as one starting at Hgx^{-1}; these are generally distinct positive x-edges. Incoming uniqueness follows from the separate edge Hgx^{-1}→Hg, so the theorem is readily repaired but the sentence is false.

Its closing sentence says the 'first two clauses' are AB1, which reads as including additivity, while rem-the-axiom-labels-and-where-they-come-from explicitly says additivity is unnumbered and AB1 is only the kernel-cokernel clause. The mathematical definition is clear, but the axiom label is internally inconsistent.
